findings.title: The overwrite guard is on a write path that `sq review code` never uses
findings.description:
T12 adds archive-on-overwrite only to `save_review_file` (`persistence.py:220-254`). But the CLI writes reviews through `save_review_result`: `cli/commands/review.py:451, 523, 610, 746` (line 746 is `sq review code`). The pipeline's main path also uses `save_review_result` (`pipeline/actions/review.py:255`). `save_review_file` is only reached by the pipeline's no-slice-info fallback (`pipeline/actions/review.py:272`). `save_review_result` calls `path.write_text` directly at lines 300 and 303.

So after T12/T13, re-running `sq review code <N>` still destroys hand edits without warning. That leaves two success criteria unmet: "Re-running `sq review code <N>` … archives the prior content" and the F003 fail-closed criterion. The slice design names `save_review_file`, but the success criteria name the real command, and the tasks have to meet the criteria.

`save_review_result` also has no "return `None` on failure" contract. It returns `Path` and raises, so T12's "matching the function's existing failure-return contract" doesn't carry over. The fix:
- Put the guard in a shared helper called by both writers (or have `save_review_result` delegate to the guarded write).
- Define what `save_review_result` does on an aborted overwrite.
- Have T13 test through `save_review_result`, or through the `sq review code` CLI path.

findings.title: The Part 0 move makes `review/` import `pipeline/`, the exact cycle F002 was meant to remove
findings.description:
T1 moves `models.py` "verbatim", but it imports `squadron.pipeline.models.ActionResult` (line 14), which `read_findings` uses (line 93). T3 moves `verification.py`, which imports `RoundDiff` from `pipeline.actions.findings_addressed.screens` (`verification.py:17`). T3 calls that import "pipeline→review". It isn't: once moved, `review/addressed/verification.py` imports `pipeline`, which is review→pipeline. T5's `judge_residue_core` takes `diff: RoundDiff` too (today's `judge.py:21`), so the moved judge core inherits the same import.

After Part 0 as written, `review/addressed/` depends on `pipeline/` in three places. That's the package-level cycle the slice design's "Dependency direction (review F002)" section exists to prevent. Pyright and the 305 suite won't catch it, so T2/T4/T6/T8 would all pass.

The tasks need to:
- Move the `RoundDiff` dataclass (not `compute_round_diff`/screens) into `review/addressed/`, or into a neutral module.
- Leave the `ActionResult`-based `read_findings` adapter in the pipeline package, or have it take the raw findings list instead.
- Add a check, such as a grep or test, that nothing under `src/squadron/review/` imports `squadron.pipeline`.

findings.title: The cf archive-scanning check comes after Part D's commit, not before
findings.description: The slice design's Phase 5 note says the cf `archive/` verification must be "sequenced before Part D lands" because it decides the filename scheme. T14 comes after T12 and T13, and T13's commit line (line 272) commits Part D before T14 runs. T12 and T14 each try to make up for this with "do not mark done until…" text. Since a checkbox can't block a commit, the fix is to move T14 ahead of T12.

findings.title: Only one of the two persistence paths gets a `reviewedSha` test, and T10 is vague about where HEAD is resolved
findings.description:
Success criterion 1 requires `reviewedSha` "from both the CLI and the pipeline persistence paths". T11 tests one of them, "whichever is more directly testable", so the other goes unproven.

T10 also doesn't match the code:
- The pipeline's main path already goes through `save_review_result` (line 255). Resolving HEAD in both `save_review_result` and the pipeline action would run it twice for that path.
- The fallback path calls `format_review_markdown` directly (line 265) and needs the SHA passed in there.
- `save_review_result` has no `cwd` parameter, yet T10 writes `run_git([...], cwd=...)`.

T10 should name one helper that resolves HEAD (DRY), show where it is called on each of the three write sites, and T11 should test both entry points.

findings.title: A second re-run overwrites the earlier archive copy without warning
findings.description:
T12 archives to `archive/{original filename}` with no collision handling. Here's how content gets lost:
1. Edit a review, then re-run: the edited v1 goes to `archive/`.
2. Edit v2, then re-run again: `archive/{name}` is replaced, and the edited v1 is gone with no warning.

That breaks success criterion 7's "nothing is silently destroyed". Add a non-colliding archive name (for example a timestamp or `-a{n}` suffix, compatible with T14's possible renaming) and a test that re-saves twice.

Also, derive the archive directory from the review file's own parent (`path.parent / "archive"`) rather than the cwd-relative literal `project-documents/user/reviews/archive/`. Otherwise tmp-dir fixtures and the `reviews_dir=` override would archive into the wrong place.

findings.title: An aborted overwrite doesn't keep the new review's content
findings.description: The design's Part D says that on abort "the review content is still printed to the terminal". T12 only returns `None` and logs an ERROR. On the CLI path, that means a fresh review that cost a model call disappears when the archive fails. Add the content-preserving behavior to T12 and an assertion for it to T13's abort test.

findings.title: Commit markers and the baseline wording are a bit off
findings.description:
- Commit lines are written as `Commit:` bullets inside tasks rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines. They do sit at tested points.
- Part 0 has four refactor commits. That's fine, but they could be merged into one, since only the end state needs to be green.
- T8 says the expected count is "2832 passed … plus this slice's later additions", but no additions exist by T8. It should just say "unchanged from the 305 baseline".
